products.quality: Two-stage: permanent lens-distortion calibration (presets for official cameras) then camera-to-workspace alignment via engraved targets; must re-run alignment if the camera moves. Thorough, guided, but finicky—alignment-score quality matters.

No camera. CNC-only router software; positions by manual zeroing to a workpiece corner/center. Docs site carries only hidden shared-with-LightBurn camera-calibration pages, not an exposed MillMage feature.
No camera support of any kind, so no calibration. Long-standing user feature requests (GitHub #2385, #74) remain unimplemented; the app targets basic GRBL sending.

Camera-first UX with per-machine guided calibrations: manual camera calibration (M1), distant-view/close-view calibration (P2/P3), and Aimed-Measure calibration. Calibration is a core onboarding step, not an add-on.
No camera. XY work-zero is set by manually jogging to the material's front-left corner; only a Z-probe accessory (for Z zero) exists—nothing to calibrate optically.

Live camera overlay places designs on real material; accuracy is hardware-bound (mount stability, camera MP)—fine for general placement, sub-mm needs care. Fine-tune via Width/Height/X-Y-Shift. 2.1 adds multi/IP-camera support.
No camera overlay. Output is positioned relative to a chosen workpiece corner/center set during Project Setup with manual X/Y zeroing—no on-screen live view of the work material.

No camera overlay—the single most-cited missing feature versus LightBurn; users must frame by watching the head move. Third-party cameras (e.g. Mintion) provide monitoring only, not positioning overlay.

Signature strength—camera-first WYSIWYG placement. Single wide camera ~1.5mm (M1, ≤3mm material); P2 dual-camera close-view reaches ~0.3mm via Aimed Measure. Accuracy degrades with material un-flatness/height.
No camera and no live view of the work material; placement is entirely by manual work-zero jogging plus homing. No camera-overlay positioning surface at all.
Camera capture-to-vector is built into the Cameras workflow: trace artwork or objects placed in the laser directly from a camera image into editable vectors. Standard, documented feature.
No camera, so no capture-to-vector. It inherits LightBurn's design tools (bitmap trace exists) but only from imported image files, never from a live camera.
No camera. It has a file-based raster→vector vectorization tool, but nothing is captured from a camera; camera support is entirely absent.
Camera-equipped machines capture the baseplate image; users trace/outline real objects to vectors (Trace: auto-trace/centerline). Camera-less machines fall back to a phone-photo snapshot import.
No camera. Image trace is available only from uploaded image files via the import workflow, not from any live camera capture.

Full Print-and-Cut: two Target Positions (Tools→Print and Cut→Set First/Second Target Location) measure offset, rotation and scale to align a cut to printed media; requires Absolute Coords; accuracy grows with target separation.
No print-and-cut / registration-mark alignment. Registration to a workpiece is done by probing or manual origin-setting, not by aligning to printed marks.
No print-and-cut or registration-mark workflow; the app lacks LightBurn's advanced alignment features. Inferred absent from the feature set and comparison write-ups.

evidence.cite: https://lasergrbl.com/usage/ (feature not present in documented usage index)

products.quality: 'Print & blade cut' registers printed patterns for blade-module machines (e.g. M1); the camera also positions a laser cut onto pre-printed material. Capability is machine/module dependent.
No print-and-cut / registration-mark workflow. Machine control is limited to manual work-zero plus homing; nothing aligns a cut to printed artwork.

evidence.cite: https://support.easel.com/hc/en-us (no print-and-cut article in support catalog)

products.quality: Print-and-Cut doubles as a jig/fixture workflow—align a project to existing target marks on a fixture for repeat placement—and the camera overlay enables eyeball repeat placement. No dedicated fixture library.

CNC-native analog: a Probing Wizard (XYZ probe block on a workpiece corner) sets origin plus a work offset for repeatable fixture/jig placement. Probe/manual-based—no camera or board-outline auto-capture.
No fixture/board-capture or jig workflow; repeatability relies on manual origin/zero setting only. No camera and no repeat-placement tooling.

evidence.cite: https://lasergrbl.com/usage/ (no fixture/jig feature in usage index)

products.quality: Camera captures the full baseplate; Batch Fill / Smart Fill replicate a design across multiple identical pieces placed on the bed for repeat/batch production—a camera-driven fixture-style placement workflow.
No jig/board-capture feature. Repeatable placement depends on homing plus manually re-setting the same work zero; there is no fixture or board-capture tool.
